About The Assignment

Background 

At Thales, a project is currently ongoing to migrate away from the currently used Maven build system to Bazel for increased build performance, more granular caching, better parallelism and more deterministic artifacts. The current work for the Bazel migration project mainly consists of adopting or creating Bazel variants of the tools used within the different departments to build software components, systems and applications. One of these tools called Cucumber is used to run behavior driven integration tests. This is used to run containerized integration tests of software components using Podman containers in an environment similar to an actual deployment environment.

One of the advantages of Bazel is its highly efficient parallel execution of so-called actions, which include tests. However, this is currently conflicting with the limits of our integration test setup, mainly due to the limitations of Podman being single-threaded and non-reentrant which is at best unreliable when run in parallel, or will simply fail. This requires that parallel execution is disabled for these tests, significantly increasing build time and reducing part of the advantage that Bazel provides.

Assignment 

It needs to be investigated what options are available within the closed Thales environment to fully parallelize containerized integration tests when using Bazel as the build system, Podman as the container orchestrator and Cucumber as the integration testing framework.

The goal for this assignment is to create a proof-of-concept of an improved testing infrastructure capable of running containerized integration tests in parallel. The PoC needs to adhere to the following:

Support Bazel as the build system (working with Maven is a nice to have)

Uses Podman as the container orchestrator

Uses the current testing infrastructure as a base

Uses Cucumber as the integration testing framework

No tests shall require the ‘exclusive’ flag, which forces given tests to run sequentially.

Ideally, no test shall require the ‘flaky’ flag, which executes a test ‘n’ number of times, where the test is considered as passed so long as one of the attempts passes. Since this is also highly dependent on the tests themselves, this is not a hard requirement.

Its mission is to help teachers deliver joyful, effective learning moments and support one million teachers worldwide, making a positive impact on the next generation of learners.

LessonUp is looking for a Senior Platform Automation Engineer to take ownership of its cloud platform, strengthen production infrastructure, and improve developer productivity.

This role focuses on platform engineering, DevOps, and infrastructure rather than writing day-to-day QA tests. You will manage and improve the company's Google Cloud Platform (GCP) environment, address technical debt, maintain reliable production systems, and build the infrastructure and CI/CD workflows that help developers deliver and validate code more quickly.

A key part of the role is enabling isolated, temporary environments for every pull request and ensuring automated end-to-end tests run reliably within CI pipelines. You will work closely with developers and QA engineers to improve testing workflows, reduce flaky test results, and support faster, more dependable releases.

•Take ownership of the production GCP environment, addressing technical debt and managing cloud resources.
•Improve infrastructure security, performance, scalability, reliability, and cost efficiency.
•Design, implement, and maintain ephemeral environments for individual pull requests so teams can test and review changes in isolation.
•Operate end-to-end testing frameworks, including Playwright, Jest, and Cucumber, within CI pipelines.
•Improve test execution by integrating testing into ephemeral environments, optimising parallelisation, and reducing flaky results.
•Streamline CI/CD pipelines, build processes, and deployment workflows to reduce developer waiting time.
•Establish reliable release processes that support consistent and dependable production deployments.
•Provide APIs, data-preparation tools, and CI/CD integrations that help developers and QA engineers build, maintain, and run their own test suites.
•Balance production infrastructure needs with internal tooling and the wider engineering team's requirements.

•At least 8 years of experience primarily in Platform Engineering, DevOps, or Site Reliability Engineering (SRE).
•At least 2 years of experience in a senior role.
•Strong experience managing production cloud infrastructure, developer tooling, and CI/CD pipelines.
•Strong proficiency with Google Cloud Platform (GCP).
•Experience with infrastructure as code (IaC) and scalable production environments.
•Practical experience operating end-to-end testing frameworks within CI pipelines, including test integration, parallelisation, and flakiness reduction.
•Comfort working with GraphQL APIs and MongoDB databases.
•Ability to work independently, make pragmatic and data-driven decisions, and take ownership of platform initiatives.
•A proactive, curious, open-minded, and collaborative approach to working with engineering teams.

Preferred Qualifications

•Experience with Terraform for infrastructure as code.
•Familiarity with Cucumber for behaviour-driven development (BDD).
•Experience with Storybook.

•Choice of a 32-, 36-, or 40-hour working week.
